name: Gnostic Christian schools

citations.excerpt: This first came into prominence in the opening decades of the 2nd century A.D. , but is certainly older; it reached its height in the second third of the same century, and began to wane about the 3rd century
Offshoots of it, however, continued on into the 4th and 5th centuries.

facts.value: A religious movement alongside the early church, defined as a syncretism with strong Christian influences, divided by Schaff into Alexandrian and Syrian families.

citations.excerpt: which may roughly be defined as a distinct religious syncretism bearing the strong impress of Christian influences.
Geographically they may be reduced to two great families, the Egyptian or Alexandrian, and the Syrian, which are also intrinsically different.

research_notes: Umbrella grouping, not a single body. Scholarship since 1945 (Nag Hammadi) has revised much; ODCC check needed.
